approval.cost: No fee for the GA APIs or verification is stated in the documentation read (the official pages read also do not publish the sensitivity classification of analytics.readonly/analytics.edit; it is surfaced in the Cloud Console when scopes are added)
approval.trigger: The gate is Google's platform-wide OAuth app verification (the shared Google layer), not a GA-specific review, and there is no GA app listing/marketplace. While the consent screen is in Testing publishing status, only users on the test-user list can authorize, and refresh tokens are short-lived (7 days, see Blockers). Per Google's OAuth App Verification help, if an app starts using new sensitive or restricted scopes before verification, 'your app's users will experience the unverified app screen and the app will be subject to the 100-user cap', and Google recommends getting verified before shipping scope changes. Verifying removes the warning screen and the cap. Scope-change trap: adding new sensitive scopes to an already-verified production project re-triggers the unverified-app screen and 100-user cap until the new scopes are approved; Google explicitly recommends testing new scopes in a separate project first.
approval.wait: Not stated in the documentation read (Google's general sensitive-scope verification figures live in the Google guide; no GA-specific timeline is published)

blockers.detail: The token acts as the consenting user; if that user lacks (or loses) a role on the GA property, calls fail even with a valid token. Per the quickstart: 'In the Google Analytics UI, grant your user account access to a Google Analytics property.' Connection health depends on the customer's GA access management, not just token state.
blockers.howToClear: Check property access at connect time and surface a clear re-grant path when calls start failing.
blockers.title: Consent is not access

blockers.detail: 'A Google Cloud Platform project with an OAuth consent screen configured for an external user type and a publishing status of Testing is issued a refresh token expiring in 7 days' (unless the only scopes are a subset of userinfo.email/userinfo.profile/openid). GA scopes are not in the exempt subset, so a Testing-mode GA integration re-breaks weekly.
blockers.howToClear: Move the consent screen to In production and complete verification before real users connect.
blockers.title: Testing-status refresh tokens expire in 7 days

blockers.detail: Data API usage is metered in tokens per property (Core, Realtime, Funnel, Chat categories). Standard property: Core 200,000 tokens/property/day, 40,000/hour, of which 14,000/hour per project per property; 10 concurrent requests per property; Analytics 360 properties get 10x. Quota is consumed against the CUSTOMER's property, shared across every tool querying it, so your reporting competes with the customer's other tools (including Google's own connectors).
blockers.howToClear: Budget queries against the property quota, cache reports, and treat the 14,000/hour project slice as the design limit.
blockers.title: Property quota is a commons

alternatives: Service account (no user consent flow; each customer must add the service account's email as a user on their GA property; the official quickstart demonstrates runReport this way and notes you 'can authenticate with a user account or service account'). A legitimate documented connection model, often simpler for reporting tools, but it puts a manual per-customer step (adding the SA email in the GA UI) in the onboarding path and cannot be initiated from your product's connect flow
flavor.recommended: A Web application OAuth client in a Google Cloud project (authorization code flow with access_type=offline), requesting the narrowest GA scope that fits
flavor.why: There is no GA-specific app object. The object is a standard Google Cloud project containing an OAuth 2.0 client ID (created in Google API Console / Google Auth Platform) plus an OAuth consent screen; Google Analytics is reached by enabling the GA APIs on that project and requesting GA scopes. Scope sets differ by API surface: for reporting (GA4), https://www.googleapis.com/auth/analytics.readonly ('See and download your Google Analytics data'); for configuration/management, https://www.googleapis.com/auth/analytics.edit ('Edit Google Analytics management entities'). The Google Analytics Admin API v1beta has only analytics.edit and analytics.readonly; the legacy Google Analytics API v3 family adds analytics, analytics.manage.users, analytics.manage.users.readonly, analytics.provision, and analytics.user.deletion. The Data API is GA4-only; mixing v3 scopes into a GA4 app adds consent/verification surface for nothing.

humanMust: Create or select a Google Cloud project
Enable the API(s): Google Analytics Data API v1 and/or Google Analytics Admin API (separate APIs, enabled separately)
Configure the OAuth consent screen (app name, support email, scopes; test users if staying in Testing)
Create the OAuth client (Clients > Create Client > Web application; authorized redirect URIs; download client_secret.json and store it securely)
For production with sensitive scopes: set the consent screen to In production and complete Google OAuth verification
name: Google Analytics
nuances: Refresh-token cliff edges (production): no fixed expiry, but a refresh token stops working if the user revokes the app's access, if it 'has not been used for six months', on password change (Gmail scopes), on time-based access expiry, or by admin policy. Hard cap: 'There is currently a limit of 100 refresh tokens per Google Account per OAuth 2.0 client ID. If the limit is reached, creating a new refresh token automatically invalidates the oldest refresh token without warning', so heavy re-consent/testing under one user's account silently kills their oldest connection; dormant customers will need to reconnect.

Shared GA API limits (excluding Data API calls): 50,000 requests per project per day; 10 queries per second per IP address; exceeding quota returns error 403 or 429. Admin API: 1,200 requests/minute; 600 requests/minute per user; 600 writes/minute; 180 writes/minute per user; 500 user deletions per day per property.
Access-token lifetime is per-response (expires_in, 'The remaining lifetime of the access token in seconds'; Google's sample response shows 3920). No fixed GA-specific lifetime is published.

Two APIs, two enablements, overlapping scopes: Data API (GA4 reporting, runReport targets properties/{propertyId}) and Admin API (configuration) are separate products; enable and scope each deliberately.

tagline: Not a separate app at all: a Google Cloud OAuth client asking for Analytics scopes, inheriting Google's verification machinery, with two GA-specific traps. Consent does not grant property access, and the Data API quota is charged against the customer's property, shared with every other tool they use.
